title: Input distance and consistency-test rejection
statement: Let $C$ be a Boolean circuit on $n$ input bits, where $n>0$, let $p$ be a Boolean proof word of the prescribed length for $C$, and let $w,w_0\in\{0,1\}^n$. Suppose that for every input coordinate, the affine-coordinate correction derived from the quadratic proof table of $p$ returns the sign encoding of the corresponding bit of $w_0$ with probability at least $1/2$. Then one half the relative Hamming distance between $w$ and $w_0$ is at most one minus the acceptance probability of the circuit's input-consistency tester on the concatenation of $w$ and $p$.
hypotheses_covered: A Boolean circuit on n input bits with n>0
A Boolean proof word of the prescribed circuit-dependent length
Two input words w and w₀
For every coordinate, the specified affine-coordinate correction probability for w₀ is at least 1/2
